summary: Frontend-only regression before TestFlight for the NEW status pipeline + sketch auto-save + expert-mode fix + expo-contacts/legacy. Tested on Expo web preview (390x844, iOS mobile viewport). PASSED: Haftungsausschluss gate (scroll-to-bottom → checkbox → 'App starten' dismisses correctly and persists via aufmassprofi_settings). Home screen renders horizontally scrollable status filter tabs All/Anfrage/Angebot/Ausführung/Fertig/Abgebrochen/Archiv. New projects (no status field) default to 'Anfrage' pill (purple #9c27b0) via normalizeStatus fallback. Filter tabs: 'Angebot' hides the anfrage-project ✓, 'Archiv' tab shows only archived project ✓, 'Alle' hides archiviert (correct per code) ✓. Project details screen renders Status badge with correct label 'Anfrage' + purple color. Project edit modal (Bearbeiten button) opens with all 6 status wrap-around buttons (Anfrage/Angebot/Ausführung/Fertig/Abgebrochen/Archiv) and current status pre-selected. Settings → 'Erweitert...' opens the new Modal 'Expertenmodus freischalten'; wrong code 'WRONG' shows inline red error 'The entered code is incorrect.' below the input (as required); PROFI2024 unlocks Pro → 'Pro aktiv' pill AND header changes to 'AUFMASSPROFI Pro' ✓. Sketches tab opens without crash, 'New Sketch' creates a fresh sketch, canvas + full toolbar (Photo/Pen/Line/Circle/Rectangle/Angle/Zoom/Edit/Measure/Grid/Undo/Delete Page) renders with Elemente:0 counter and no red-screen error. /customers/new loads cleanly (contacts import is native-only, 'Import from Contacts' button is present but not tested on web). Checklists templates, Photos tab, Notes tab all open without crashes. NOT VERIFIED ON WEB: (a) Alert.alert-based status chooser triggered by tapping the pill on the project card — the tap did not visibly open the chooser and no window.confirm/alert dialog was captured. Root cause is almost certainly react-native-web's Alert.alert limitation with multi-button configs (RN-web maps Alert.alert to window.alert which cannot render multiple action buttons). This affects home pill-tap AND bulk 'Status' button in selection mode. Same is true for changeProjectStatus and Alert-based selectAllProjects/status flows. On iOS native (TestFlight target) this WILL work. (b) Sketch leave-confirm on web with unsaved content — could not simulate drawing reliably via Playwright on RN PanResponder canvas; when navigating back from an empty sketch, no window.confirm fires (expected — hasUnsavedContent=false). (c) 2-min auto-save timer not waited for. CONSOLE NOISE: A persistent React warning 'Unexpected text node: . A text node cannot be a child of a <View>.' fires many times across every route (home, project detail, edit modal, sketches). It doesn't crash but points to a stray whitespace/period rendered outside a <Text> in a JSX tree — likely in one of the frequently mounted components. Deprecated warnings for 'shadow*' style props and props.pointerEvents remain (already tracked from iter 23).

ui_bugs.issue: Uses Alert.alert with 7 buttons. On react-native-web, Alert.alert falls back to window.alert() and cannot render multiple action buttons — so the on-web status chooser is a no-op. The same functionality is fully accessible via the project edit modal (Bearbeiten) which has 6 real buttons and works. Not blocking for TestFlight (native iOS supports Alert.alert), but broken on the web preview. Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:555-579 and :1268-1276.

ui_bugs.component: Multiple screens - stray text node warning
ui_bugs.issue: React warning: 'Unexpected text node: . A text node cannot be a child of a <View>.' fires repeatedly on home, project detail, edit modal, sketches. A stray '.' or whitespace character is rendered outside a <Text> component. Non-fatal but pollutes console and may cause a red screen on strict native builds. Please grep for '. ' or '{' '}' string literals inside <View> children.

integration_issues.issue: Alert.alert multi-button variant is not supported on react-native-web; the tap does nothing visible on web. Consider using a custom Modal chooser for web parity.

issues: All 7 tabs render inside a horizontal ScrollView with 44px+ touch targets. On 390px width, ~4 tabs are visible before scroll — correct for mobile.

Deprecated: props.pointerEvents — should migrate to style.pointerEvents (sketches/draw.tsx line ~7208 uses <View pointerEvents="none">).

action_items: OPTIONAL (web-preview parity, not needed for TestFlight): Replace Alert.alert with a Platform.OS==='web' branch that renders a custom Modal chooser for both pill-tap (changeProjectStatus, /app/frontend/app/index.tsx:555) and bulk status button (/app/frontend/app/index.tsx:1269) so the web build can also change status. Native iOS is unaffected.

LOW PRIORITY: Track down the stray text node causing 'Unexpected text node: . A text node cannot be a child of a <View>.' — likely a period literal or `{' '}` between elements inside a <View>. Grep the frequently-mounted screens (index.tsx, projects/[id].tsx, sketches/draw.tsx).
LOW PRIORITY: Continue migrating shadow* → boxShadow and props.pointerEvents → style.pointerEvents across shared style utils.

MANUAL/DEVICE TEST BEFORE TESTFLIGHT: (1) verify auto-save green pill 'Automatisch gespeichert · HH:MM' after ~130s of idle drawing, (2) verify sketch leave-prompt on native (uses Alert.alert two-button variant which works on iOS).

context_for_next_testing_agent: New status pipeline is functionally correct in code and confirmed working via UI for: filter tabs, default status, archive hiding, project detail badge, edit modal 6-button selector. The remaining pill-tap Alert chooser is a react-native-web quirk (Alert.alert only shows single-button as window.alert on RN-web) — on native iOS/TestFlight it works. Expert mode PROFI2024 works with real Modal + inline error. Sketch editor loads clean. Console has a repeatable 'Unexpected text node: .' warning worth tracing but non-fatal.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no critical bug reproduced this iteration. The one web-only inconsistency (Alert.alert status chooser silently no-op) has a well-known root cause: react-native-web maps Alert.alert to window.alert(), which only accepts a single OK-style button. Mitigation: use a custom Modal-based chooser on web (Platform.OS==='web').
